body.statement: At \(P\in\mathcal P_4^{\circ}\), suppose the finite-dimensional local experiments generated by finite collections of scores from the tangent score space are locally asymptotically normal, and suppose an estimator sequence is regular relative to all those experiments. If \(\theta\) is pathwise differentiable with canonical gradient \(D\) in the closure of that score space, then every weak limit law of the centered estimator sequence is the convolution of \(N(0,E_P[D(O)^2])\) and another probability law. In particular, whenever its asymptotic variance exists, it is at least \(V_P=E_P[D(O)^2]\).

source.verbatim_statement: Suppose that the sequence of experiments is locally asymptotically normal and that the estimator sequence is regular. Then its limit distribution is the convolution of the efficient normal distribution and another probability distribution.

attestation.note: Transcribed from van der Vaart (1998), Theorem 25.20, and specialized in the node statement to the scalar canonical gradient.
